episode.title: Resolve file edits against one observable absolute workspace target
episode.before: At parent 0c6e133c0434ec856d4aea2b08f216f36c0e7dac, relative file paths were joined to the live terminal cwd, TERMINAL_CWD, or process cwd without first guaranteeing that the selected base was absolute. The write and replace-patch entry points separately resolved paths for locking and staleness checks but passed the caller's original path to the lower file-operations layer. Consequently, tool-layer checks and the actual edit could resolve the same relative path from different working directories, allowing an edit intended for a worktree to land in another checkout without the successful response naming the actual target.
episode.after: At pinned ref 96643b4a52b118477b07c838e30eb8ae7372062c, relative paths use a single absolute base selected in precedence order from the task's live terminal cwd, TERMINAL_CWD, and process cwd; relative configured bases are anchored once to the process cwd. Write and replace-patch operations pass the resulting absolute target to the lower layer, successful responses expose resolved_path and files_modified, and relative targets outside an available live workspace produce a warning. Eleven focused tests cover base precedence, absolute-path preservation, divergence-warning conditions, successful write routing, successful replace-patch routing, and protection of a decoy checkout.
episode.diff: The commit adds _resolve_base_dir, rewrites _resolve_path_for_task around its absolute-base invariant, adds _path_resolution_warning, changes write_file_tool and replace-mode patch_tool to operate on pre-resolved absolute targets, enriches successful mutation responses with absolute target metadata, and adds tests/tools/test_file_tools_cwd_resolution.py. The implementation file changes by 103 insertions and 10 deletions, with 197 lines of new focused tests.

evidence_units.claim: The pinned implementation commit is 96643b4a52b118477b07c838e30eb8ae7372062c, its first parent is 0c6e133c0434ec856d4aea2b08f216f36c0e7dac, and it changes tools/file_tools.py plus a new focused test file.
The parent implementation selected a live/config/process base, joined it directly to a relative input, and called Path.resolve without an explicit invariant that the base itself was absolute.

The new base resolver gives the live task terminal cwd precedence over TERMINAL_CWD and the process cwd, anchors any relative base to os.getcwd(), resolves it, and therefore always returns an absolute base.
write_file_tool now passes its pre-resolved absolute target to file_ops.write_file instead of the original caller path; successful output includes resolved_path and a one-element files_modified list.

Replace-mode patching now passes the corresponding pre-resolved target to file_ops.patch_replace; successful patch output reports resolved modified paths and reports resolved_path for a single target.
The divergence checker returns no warning for absolute inputs, missing live cwd, or targets inside the live workspace, but names both locations when a relative input resolves outside that workspace.
The write and patch call sites add the divergence warning after higher-priority cross-agent and per-task staleness warnings, so existing warnings retain precedence.
evidence_units.source: git show 96643b4a52b118477b07c838e30eb8ae7372062c:tools/file_tools.py, write_file_tool and patch_tool warning selection

evidence_units.claim: At the pinned ref, the shared path resolver is also used by file-operation lookup, sensitive-path and profile checks, reads, timestamp tracking, and staleness checks, making the absolute-base contract common to those consumers.

Five tests establish base behavior: relative TERMINAL_CWD is anchored absolutely, live tracking wins, an absolute configured cwd is honored, absolute input is not re-anchored, and absent configuration falls back to an absolute process cwd.
Four tests establish the warning boundary: warn for a relative target outside the live workspace, but not for an inside target, an absolute input, or absence of a live cwd.
The write regression test asserts that a relative write modifies the live workspace, returns its absolute resolved_path, and returns the same path in files_modified.

The replace-patch regression test asserts that a relative patch modifies the live workspace, reports its absolute target, and leaves the identically named file in a decoy process-cwd checkout untouched.

The commit message reports 11 new unit tests, 43 live end-to-end assertions, and 466 existing file/path/terminal tests passing; only the committed focused-test source was directly inspectable in this environment.

The focused suite could not be executed in the provided checkout because the pytest executable is unavailable, and the checkout HEAD is 9a6108fdf29bb789520fd5b10f9cb01a2cbf311d rather than the pinned ref.
evidence_units.source: local commands: pytest -q tests/tools/test_file_tools_cwd_resolution.py; git rev-parse HEAD

candidate_atomics.name: establish-absolute-resolution-base
candidate_atomics.title: Establish one absolute base for relative paths
candidate_atomics.description: Choose the authoritative runtime directory using explicit precedence and canonicalize it before appending any relative target.

semantic_action.intent: Prevent relative file targets from changing meaning across tool layers or resolution time because their base is itself relative or stale.
semantic_action.pre_state: A file target may be relative, and the available live terminal cwd, configured terminal cwd, or process cwd may disagree or include a relative value.
semantic_action.post_state: Every relative target is resolved from one deterministic absolute base; live task cwd is authoritative when available, while absolute input targets remain unanchored to that base.
semantic_action.validation: Exercise every base-precedence branch and assert absolute, expected targets, including preservation of absolute inputs.

candidate_atomics.name: propagate-canonical-mutation-target
candidate_atomics.title: Use and report the same canonical mutation target
candidate_atomics.description: Pass the already resolved absolute target to the mutation layer and expose it in successful results so execution, coordination, and reporting agree.

semantic_action.intent: Eliminate disagreement between the path checked or locked by the tool layer and the path actually edited by a lower layer with a different working directory.
semantic_action.module_role: File mutation orchestration and result reporting boundary
semantic_action.pre_state: The orchestration layer has resolved a target for locking and checks, but the lower mutation layer could still receive and independently interpret the original relative path.
semantic_action.post_state: Supported write and replace-patch mutations receive the canonical target, and successful output identifies the same absolute target through resolved_path and files_modified.
semantic_action.validation: Write and replace-patch a relative target with distinct workspace and process-cwd copies; assert the workspace copy changes, the decoy remains unchanged for patching, and response paths equal the edited absolute path.

candidate_atomics.name: surface-workspace-target-divergence
candidate_atomics.title: Warn when a relative target escapes the active workspace
candidate_atomics.description: Compare a resolved relative target with the authoritative live workspace and surface an explanatory warning without changing absolute-path semantics or overriding stronger warnings.

semantic_action.intent: Make a wrong-checkout destination visible on the first mutation response when the system can identify an authoritative active workspace.
semantic_action.pre_state: A caller supplied a relative path, an absolute resolved target is known, and a live workspace root may be available for comparison.
semantic_action.post_state: Targets outside an available live workspace produce a warning naming the resolved target and workspace; inside targets, absolute inputs, and cases without a live root do not produce this warning.
semantic_action.validation: Assert the warning matrix for outside, inside, absolute-input, and no-live-root cases, and inspect call sites to confirm staleness warnings retain priority.

candidate_atomics.name: verify-workspace-routing-contract
candidate_atomics.title: Verify routing and observability with a decoy checkout
candidate_atomics.description: Model divergent workspace and process directories and assert resolution, warning, mutation, response, and isolation invariants.

semantic_action.intent: Detect regressions where a relative edit succeeds against a different checkout than the active workspace or conceals its actual destination.
semantic_action.pre_state: The path-resolution and mutation changes are implemented, and tests can create distinct active-workspace and process-cwd files with the same relative name.
semantic_action.post_state: The test oracle covers base precedence, warning applicability, correct write and replace-patch routing, absolute response metadata, and non-modification of the decoy patch target.
semantic_action.validation: Run the focused 11-test module and then the broader file/path/terminal suites; require all routing assertions and existing compatibility tests to pass.

candidate_workflows.name: resolve-and-observe-workspace-file-mutations
candidate_workflows.title: Keep relative file mutations anchored to the active workspace
candidate_workflows.description: A partial-order workflow for repairing file tools whose coordination checks and actual mutations can interpret relative paths from different roots, especially across a main checkout and a worktree.

workflow_graph.goal: Ensure a relative file mutation is resolved, executed, coordinated, and reported against one absolute target associated with the task's active workspace, while making detectable divergence visible.
when_to_use: A tool resolves or checks a relative file path before delegating the actual mutation to another component that may have a different working directory.
A process can operate in one checkout while a task terminal or worktree operates in another.
Successful mutation responses do not currently reveal the absolute on-disk target, making wrong-root edits difficult to diagnose.
anti_goals: Do not infer that every relative configured cwd identifies the intended workspace; canonicalization makes it deterministic, while live task cwd supplies workspace authority when available.
Do not re-anchor caller-supplied absolute paths under the active workspace.
Do not turn the workspace-divergence diagnostic into a blanket prohibition against intentional outside-workspace absolute paths.
Do not replace or lower the priority of existing concurrency and staleness diagnostics.
Do not broaden this workflow into redesigning file contents, patch matching, or general filesystem authorization.
not_applicable_when: All mutation APIs require absolute paths and no layer independently reinterprets them.
The system has no task-specific or configured root concept and deliberately defines relative paths solely against one immutable process cwd.
The observed failure is caused by patch-content mismatch, permissions, or filesystem errors rather than disagreement about the path root.
inputs: Live task terminal cwd when available
Lower mutation operation and its result object
Focused test environment containing separate intended and decoy roots
workflow_graph.entry_state: At least one mutation path can be relative, and path checks, locks, lower-level execution, or response reporting may not share one canonical target.
workflow_graph.exit_state: Relative targets derive from one absolute base; supported mutations consume the resolved target; successful results expose actual absolute targets; detectable relative-path escapes are warned; focused routing tests establish that intended files change and decoy files do not.

steps.condition: A caller path is relative or shared consumers require canonical path identity.
steps.validation: Base-precedence tests prove live cwd authority, deterministic anchoring of relative configuration, absolute fallback, and preservation of absolute inputs.

steps.condition: A lower mutation layer can resolve relative paths independently or successful output lacks the actual target.
steps.validation: Write and replace-patch tests prove that response metadata matches the absolute edited target and that the decoy patch target remains unchanged.

steps.condition: An authoritative live workspace root is available and relative targets may legitimately resolve outside it because of stale or divergent state.
steps.validation: The warning matrix proves that only relative targets outside an available live workspace warn, while call-site inspection proves stronger existing warnings remain preferred.

steps.condition: Always validate canonical routing; warning assertions apply when the optional diagnostic is implemented.
steps.validation: Run the focused routing suite with distinct workspace and decoy roots, followed by relevant existing file/path/terminal tests.

validation_ladder: Statically compare parent and pinned resolver behavior to establish the former relative-base boundary and the new absolute-base invariant.
Run unit tests for base precedence and absolute-input preservation.
Run warning-boundary tests for outside, inside, absolute-input, and unavailable-live-root cases.
Run mutation tests with intended and decoy roots, asserting both changed and unchanged files plus absolute result metadata.
Run the broader existing file/path/terminal suites to check compatibility with other resolver consumers and warning precedence.
stop_conditions: Stop if no authoritative ordering among live task cwd, configured cwd, and process cwd can be established for the host system.
Stop if the lower mutation API cannot accept a canonical absolute target without changing its documented semantics; define that contract before proceeding.
Stop and investigate if coordination checks and actual mutation still identify different targets after canonicalization.
Do not declare validation complete if only response metadata passes while the intended-versus-decoy filesystem assertions fail.
Defer full promotion when the focused and compatibility suites cannot be executed in the available environment.
unresolved_or_deferred: The committed tests directly exercise write_file and replace-mode patch routing; equivalent execution routing for multi-file V4A patch content is not established by the focused test file.
The commit message's 43 live end-to-end assertions and 466 passing existing tests were not independently rerun because pytest is unavailable in the provided environment.
The checkout HEAD differs from the pinned implementation ref, so evidence was obtained with git show, git diff, and git grep rather than by altering the user's working tree.

unresolved_questions: Does the lower V4A patch implementation independently anchor relative paths, and what direct test proves that its actual edited targets match the paths reported by patch_tool?
Would consumers of successful write and patch responses require a compatibility review before resolved_path and files_modified become a stable public result contract?
The issue bundle lacks the PR body, reviews, status checks, comments, and timeline, so reviewer-confirmed rationale and CI results beyond the commit message remain unavailable.
